verses.text: Jeremiah finished telling all the people everything the LORD their God had sent him to tell them.
Then Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God has not sent you to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to live there.'
Baruch son of Neriah is turning you against us, so that we will be handed over to the Babylonians. Then they can kill us or take us into exile in Babylon."
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the army officers, and all the people disobeyed the LORD's command to stay in the land of Judah.
Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army officers took all the survivors of Judah who had come back to live in the land of Judah from all the nations where they had been scattered.

They took the men, women, and children, the king's daughters, and everyone Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan. They also took Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They went to Egypt, because they did not obey the LORD, and they arrived at Tahpanhes.
At Tahpanhes the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"While the people of Judah are watching, take some large stones and bury them in the clay of the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes.

Then tell them, 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I will send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I will set his throne over these stones I have buried here, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.
He will come and attack Egypt. Those meant for death will die. Those meant for captivity will be taken captive. Those meant for the sword will be killed by the sword.

I will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt. He will burn the temples and carry off their gods as captives. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will leave there unharmed.
He will smash the sacred pillars at Beth Shemesh in Egypt and burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt.'"
